CHN.note: World #1 producer (~48% of global output) and #1 green-tea exporter. Exports 374 kt confirmed via UN Comtrade 2024 (China reporter, flow X). Huge domestic consumption keeps net trade modest relative to output.

IND.note: World #2 producer (Tea Board of India). Exports 250 kt confirmed via Comtrade 2024 (flow X), led by Iraq, Iran, Russia, CIS. Largest single consumer market after China.

KEN.note: World #1 black-tea exporter; KTDA smallholder system. Exports 625.6 kt confirmed via Comtrade 2024 (flow X) — Pakistan alone takes 221 kt. Exports can exceed same-year production via stocks/re-export of Mombasa-auction lots.

LKA.note: Ceylon tea; orthodox black-tea specialist. Exports 243.2 kt confirmed via Comtrade 2024 (flow X), led by Iraq, China, Azerbaijan, Iran (Sri Lanka Tea Board).

VNM.note: Vietnam did not report HS 0902 to Comtrade 2024; export ~130 kt estimated from partner-mirror (Pakistan, Egypt) + FAO IGG Tea. Bulk CTC/green tea to Pakistan, Taiwan, Russia, Middle East.

ARG.note: Low-cost mechanised black tea for blending/iced-tea. Exports 57.0 kt confirmed via Comtrade 2024 (flow X); 48.9 kt (86%) to the USA.

TUR.note: Major producer (Rize/Black Sea, CAYKUR) but among the world's highest per-capita tea consumers, so almost all output consumed domestically. Net trade near balance.

IDN.note: Indonesia tea ~130 kt output; mix of black and green. Net exporter ~25-40 kt (Russia, Malaysia, Pakistan). FAO IGG Tea estimate.

PAK.note: World #1 tea importer. Imports 244.1 kt confirmed via Comtrade 2024 (Pakistan reporter, flow M); Kenya supplies 211 kt (87%). One of the most import-dependent tea markets on earth.

EGY.note: Major importer; Kenya-dominated. Comtrade 2024 (Egypt reporter) shows Kenya ~73-80 kt of a ~95 kt market. Strong CTC black-tea consumption culture.

RUS.note: Russia did not report HS 0902 to Comtrade 2024; import ~140 kt estimated from supplier-mirror (Kenya 21.6, India, Sri Lanka, Indonesia, Vietnam) + FAO IGG Tea. Large packer/re-exporter to CIS.

USA.note: Imports 123.4 kt confirmed via Comtrade 2024 (USA reporter, flow M); Argentina 47.1 kt (iced-tea black), then India, China, Vietnam, Sri Lanka, Malawi.

GBR.note: Imports 114.2 kt confirmed via Comtrade 2024 (UK reporter, flow M); Kenya 61.4 kt (54%) — the classic UK-Kenya breakfast-blend link — then India, Malawi, Rwanda, Tanzania.

IRN.note: Iran produces ~100 kt (Gilan/Mazandaran) but consumes more; major importer. Did not report 2024; import ~65 kt estimated from supplier mirrors (India 12, Sri Lanka 10.4, Kenya 17.8).

MAR.note: Imports 79.0 kt confirmed via Comtrade 2024 (Morocco reporter, flow M); China 77.1 kt (98%) — the world's premier market for Chinese green gunpowder tea (mint-tea culture).

ARE.note: UAE (Dubai/DMCC) is a global tea RE-EXPORT hub, not a producer. Did not report 2024; throughput ~200 kt imported / ~165 kt re-exported estimated from partner mirrors.

KAZ.note: Imports 29.0 kt confirmed via Comtrade 2024 (Kazakhstan reporter, flow M); India 7.8, Russia 3.7 (re-export), Sri Lanka, Kenya. High per-capita Central-Asia consumer.

DEU.note: Germany (Hamburg) is Europe's tea trading/blending hub and re-exporter. Comtrade gross flows inflated by transit; true net imports for consumption ~75 kt with ~50 kt re-exported.

rankings.note: Exporter ranks for Kenya, China, India, Sri Lanka, Argentina confirmed from each country's own Comtrade flow-X reporting; UAE/Vietnam/Russia/Germany are re-export/non-reporter estimates. Importer ranks for Pakistan, USA, UK, Egypt, Morocco, Kazakhstan confirmed from Comtrade flow-M; UAE/Russia/Iran/Germany estimated from partner mirrors (non-reporters in 2024).

companies.name: Unilever / ekaterra (Lipton, PG Tips, Brooke Bond)
companies.note: World's largest tea business by volume; ekaterra (Lipton, PG Tips) sold by Unilever to CVC in 2022. Sources black tea heavily from Kenya (Kericho estates) and across East Africa.
companies.improve: Should split private-label from branded volumes and disclose post-CVC estate ownership in Kenya/Tanzania.

companies.name: Tata Consumer Products (Tetley, Tata Tea)
companies.note: Second-largest global tea brand owner; Tetley leads the UK/Canada. Sources Assam/Nilgiri domestically plus Kenyan CTC for blends.
companies.improve: Should quantify its share of India's 250 kt exports vs domestic-brand volumes.

companies.name: Associated British Foods - Twinings
companies.note: Twinings is a premium global blender sourcing from Kenya, India, Sri Lanka and China.
companies.improve: Should break out Twinings-specific leaf-purchase tonnage (reported within ABF Grocery).

companies.name: James Finlay
companies.note: Vertically integrated tea trader/estate owner (Swire group); sold its Kenyan estates to Sri Lankan buyers in 2024.
companies.improve: Should reflect the 2024 sale of James Finlay Kenya estates and clarify post-sale supply relationships.

companies.name: McLeod Russel India
companies.note: Historically among the world's largest bulk black-tea producers (Williamson Magor); financially distressed and has divested many gardens.
companies.improve: Should update estate count and current production after debt-driven garden sales.

companies.name: KTDA (Kenya Tea Development Agency)
companies.note: Manages ~600,000 Kenyan smallholder growers and ~60% of Kenya's tea via the Mombasa auction. The backbone of Kenya's 626 kt exports and thus of global black-tea supply.
companies.improve: Should add factory-level volume and track 2024 reform/levy changes affecting smallholder payouts.

global.note: Global tea (HS 0902), kt, made-tea basis. Production led by China (~48%) and India (~20%); FAO Intergovernmental Group on Tea. Output grows ~2%/yr while traded volume (~1.85 Mt) is flatter — most growth absorbed by Chinese/Indian domestic consumption.
